---
title: "Stick-breaking"
subtitle: "Catalog P-05 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I)"
description: "How one number, the concentration alpha, splits a unit stick into the weights of infinitely many components."
toc: false
---

Take a stick of length one. Break off a random proportion V_1 of it: that piece is the
first weight, w_1 = V_1. Break off a proportion V_2 of what is left: w_2 = V_2 (1 − V_1).
Keep going. With every V_k drawn from Beta(1, alpha), the weights (w_1, w_2, …) follow the
GEM(alpha) distribution, the weights of a Dirichlet process.

```{=html}
<div id="w-stick" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/stick-breaking.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxStick = DPX["stick-breaking"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-stick"), { alpha: 2 });
</script>
```

## What to try

- **alpha = 0.5.** The first break usually takes most of the stick:
  E[w_1] = 1/(1 + alpha) = .667 and Pr(w_1 > .5) = 0.5^alpha = .707.
- **alpha = 2, then 10.** The pieces get smaller and more numerous; at alpha = 10 no
  single piece dominates (E[w_1] = .091, Pr(w_1 > .5) = .001).
- **alpha = 100.** Hundreds of slivers; the stick behaves almost like a continuum.
- **Step** reveals the staircase one break at a time, so you can read each V_k.
- **Ranked by size** reorders the same pieces from largest to smallest.
- **x20 rows** draws twenty more sticks with the same alpha: the spread across rows is
  the uncertainty that a single draw hides.

The first piece matters for everything that follows on this site: it has the same
distribution as the population share of the cluster that a randomly chosen unit belongs
to (the size-biased weight W_SB). That is why Pr(W_SB > .5) is the paper's measure of
majority-mass dominance.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
After Broderick (MLSS 2016, Cádiz, part I; 2012 tutorial). The widget re-implements the
mathematics; no code from her R demonstrations is used. Keyboard: Tab to the controls,
arrow keys move the slider, Enter draws again.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/stick-breaking.html](../../embed/stick-breaking.html),
for example `?alpha=0.5`.
